newsitem.title: GERMANY: Court - East German farms must pay old debts.
newsitem.headline: Court - East German farms must pay old debts.

text.p: Germany's supreme court ruled on Tuesday that east German cooperative farms had to pay back about 10 billion marks ($5.8 billion) of communist-era debt.
It turned down an appeal by a cooperative farm that argued the debts were not real credits in the capitalist sense and therefore should not be considered valid.
But the Federal Constitutional Court added that repayment procedures for the cooperative farms, which say they could face ruin if forced to repay the debts, would have to be improved.
The farms argued they were often forced by state planners to take the credits to carry out many other functions like building roads, schools or public buildings in their villages.
In the Unity Treaty hammered out at high speed in 1990, Bonn assumed these credits were normal western-style loans.
Bonn has shouldered most outstanding credits for east German industry and local governments by diverting them into a repayment fund independent of the government budget.
